statements.text: One of the things we're working with them is to shorten the kill chains. We're doing a lot of stuff with artificial intelligence and machine learning to be able to do dynamic targeting. But we are seeing, and our goal is by this January from a year ago, to be able to increase 700 percent our ability to target dynamic targets in a 24-hour period.
statements.context: Hearing before the House Armed Services Committee on U.S. military posture; Rep. Escobar asks Gen. Kurilla about Task Force 99, and the general responds with its AI/ML work.

statements.text: We mentioned artificial intelligence. We mentioned robotics, precision munitions, the ability to sense the distances that have never been before done in human history. All of these things in combination are going to fundamentally change in my view the very character of war probably inside of a decade, for sure inside of 15 years. [...] And the country that optimizes those technologies for the conduct of war are likely to have decisive advantage. And that country needs to be us. So I would strongly recommend that we execute all those innovative technologies.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on the Fiscal Year 2024 Defense Budget Request, where Rep. Escobar asked General Milley about innovative technologies including additive manufacturing.
